items.quote: It is not meet so to do; for we shall sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians to the LORD our God
items.claim: Moses turns down the proposal as unfitting. His reason is that the Israelites' sacrifice to their God would be something the Egyptians consider an abomination.
items.object: proposal to sacrifice (as implied by 'so to do')
items.mechanism: religious incompatibility: Israelite sacrificial offerings are an abomination to Egyptians

items.quote: lo, shall we sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us?
items.claim: Moses warns that if the Israelites sacrificed where the Egyptians could see, the Egyptians might stone them.
items.object: Israelites sacrificing in view of Egyptians
items.mechanism: a public offense to Egyptian religious sensibilities could provoke stoning

items.quote: We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to the LORD our God, as he shall command us.
items.claim: As an alternative, Moses proposes that the Israelites travel three days into the wilderness and sacrifice there, as their God commands.
items.object: three days' journey into the wilderness to sacrifice
items.mechanism: moving far enough away to avoid Egyptian hostility while obeying divine command
